title: Wizard generate step intermittently unreliable
description: Mitigated by the Tailwind CSS migration: the wizard's document generation now authors Tailwind classes inline during structure generation instead of a separate CSS-rules-writing phase, and the second AI call only sets styles.variables (brand palette) instead of a full CSS-rules object - much shorter total output, lower truncation/omission risk. Verified: the editor-transform happy-path test (which hits the real configured AI_PROVIDER, not a mock) went from failing on live model runs before the prompt rewrite to 4/4 passes after. Residual variance remains possible if the live model picks Tailwind syntax outside the allowlist's scope (e.g. arbitrary-value shadow colors) - that surfaces as a normal invalid_operations rejection, same as any other allowlist miss, not a truncation failure.

title: Tailwind CSS migration
description: Styling moved from a custom JSON DSL (styles.rules: AI/editor-authored {selector, declarations} objects validated against CSS_PROPERTY_ALLOWLIST) to Tailwind utility classes on attributes.class, validated against a finite allowlist (tailwind_classes.py: is_allowed_tailwind_class/check_class_list, wired into operations.py's set_attribute and sanitize.py's check_attributes). New Tailwind v4 CLI build pipeline (npm run build:css): a management command materializes the class allowlist into a safelist sentinel file that is Tailwind's ONLY content source (tailwind-input.css uses source(none) plus explicit @source), since AI-chosen classes never appear in any file Tailwind could otherwise scan, and because Tailwind's default whole-project auto-scan was verified to compile any Tailwind-shaped string found anywhere (including test fixtures). Wizard document generation now authors classes inline during structure generation; the second AI call only sets the brand-color palette. The editor's per-element quick-style panel now toggles Tailwind classes instead of writing an inline style=\\" attribute (a second
area: previously undocumented styling mechanism this consolidated away). styles.rules/mediaQueries/keyframes remain in the schema and keep rendering for backward compatibility with every pre-migration Template/UserTemplate/Project row - verified end-to-end with a hand-seeded legacy document (still renders its old CSS
files: and remains editable). Docker/CI/local setup updated to build the CSS (Node 20 required - Debian bookworm's apt nodejs is too old for Tailwind v4)."

title: Public template publishing + storefront (products
description: Stripe checkout
category: UserTemplate gains is_published/public_slug (stable once set); new GET /t/<slug>/ (PublicTemplateView) renders a full standalone document server-side (apps/editor/rendering.py's public_page_html) for anonymous visitors, no editor scripts, 404 identically for nonexistent and unpublished. New apps/storefront app: Product (price_cents, optional image, optional digital_file for downloadables, validated by real magic-byte sniffing not extension/Content-Type) and Order (the permanent purchase record, created ONLY by a signature-verified Stripe webhook, never the checkout-redirect view). PaymentProvider abstraction (FakePaymentProvider/StripePaymentProvider) mirrors the existing AIProvider/FakeAIProvider swappable pattern - PAYMENT_PROVIDER defaults to fake, tests never touch the real Stripe API. Checkout always re-reads price from the DB, never trusts the client. Digital downloads are served through a token-gated view (never a static /media/ URL) with a download-count cap; the success page explicitly handles the webhook-vs-redirect race condition via a direct provider session lookup fallback instead of assuming the Order already exists. Editor UI: Publicar/Despublicar toggle in the save modal, a Productos management page (/productos/), and an Insertar producto control that adds a real product card with a working Comprar form to the page. Verified end-to-end with real Playwright runs: publish+view+unpublish, create a product with an image and PDF (owner-scoped), insert a product card, and the full anonymous checkout -> pending -> simulated webhook -> paid flow. Real Stripe test-mode keys were not available in this environment - the full real-Stripe-hosted-checkout-page round trip was not run; only the FakePaymentProvider path was verified live.

AI system prompt updated to convert watch URLs to embed URLs and use aspect-video instead of an arbitrary pb-[56.25%] hack. Verified end-to-end by re-running the exact original failing instruction against a live server and confirming a successful add_node operation with a working iframe."

Rather than hand-writing Tailwind classes into the deterministic template, routed the insert through the existing AI transform pipeline: EditorTransformView now populates EditorContext.available_products server-side from the requesting user's OWN active products (id/name/price_cents/image_url) - never client-supplied, so the model can't reference a product it doesn't own or invent an id. User explicitly chose this over a quick deterministic-Tailwind fix after being shown the tradeoff (latency/cost/variability vs instant/free/consistent).

title: Fix CSRF 403 on checkout/webhook for logged-in sessions
description: CheckoutView and StripeWebhookView are @csrf_exempt + AllowAny, but DRF's default SessionAuthentication runs its own CSRF check independent of that decorator whenever it successfully authenticates a request via session cookie - a logged-in visitor (e.g. the template owner testing their own Comprar button, as reported via screenshot showing 'CSRF Failed: CSRF token missing.' on /comprar/6/) got a 403 despite the view being explicitly csrf_exempt. Fixed with authentication_classes = [] on both views (no reason to authenticate a fully public/AllowAny request at all). Existing tests never caught this because the api/anon_api fixtures use force_authenticate, which bypasses DRF's real auth+CSRF pipeline entirely - added a regression test using a real client.login() session with enforce_csrf_checks=True, verified it 403s without the fix and 302s with it.

title: Fix fake-provider checkout stuck forever on Procesando tu pago
description: With PAYMENT_PROVIDER=fake (default, no Stripe keys configured), FakePaymentProvider marked a session paid instantly but nothing ever created the Order row - that only happens in StripeWebhookView.post, and there is no real Stripe server in dev/test to ever deliver that webhook. Reproduced live: a real logged-in browser session got permanently stuck on 'Procesando tu pago... Todavia estamos confirmando tu pago' right after the checkout CSRF fix (row 46) unblocked the redirect itself. Fixed by extracting the webhook's order-creation logic into a shared _record_order_for_session() and having CheckoutView call it directly right after session creation, ONLY when the provider is FakePaymentProvider - real Stripe checkouts are untouched, still require the actual signed webhook.

title: UI/UX: consolidate 3 drifted design-token sets into one shared stylesheet
description: UXUI.md audit found editor.css, templates/storefront/products.html+payment_config.html, and templates/storefront/success.html+checkout_cancel.html+registration/login.html+signup.html each hand-roll their OWN :root token block with similar-but-not-identical values (e.g. --border #dce3ec vs #e2e4ec, font-family Inter vs system-ui) instead of sharing one source. Fix: extract static/shared/tokens.css from editor.css's token set (most mature) and link it everywhere, deleting the duplicated declarations. Low-risk, pure CSS-variable rename, should be done before any further template additions compound the drift.

title: Multi-gateway checkout (Stripe/Mercado Pago/PayPal/Braintree/Wompi/PayU/ePayco/Bold)
description: Executed per PAYMENTS.md (deleted after this close-out - see openspec/specs/storefront/spec.md for the permanent behavioral contract, CHANGELOG.md for the shipped-feature record). Buyer picks gateway at checkout; PaymentGatewayConfig is owner-scoped and Fernet-encrypted at rest (apps/storefront/crypto.py); each gateway has real+Fake* provider pair behind GATEWAY_REGISTRY (apps/storefront/payments.py); Order gained a gateway field, uniqueness scoped per (gateway, gateway_session_id); GatewayWebhookView tries every enabled seller's credentials for a gateway until one verifies the signature. New /config/ page + /api/payment-gateway-configs/ (credentials write-only, never returned). AI product-card prompt now emits one buy-form per available_gateways entry. Verified end-to-end via a real browser click-through: /config toggle -> publish page -> click real Comprar button -> gracias page, for the Stripe fake-provider path. Confidence/verification depth varies sharply by gateway (see openspec/specs/storefront/spec.md and learnings.jsonl id 2026-07-23-15): Stripe/Mercado Pago/Wompi/PayU/ePayco have local HMAC/checksum signature tests (accept+reject); PayPal/Braintree tested with mocked network/SDK calls; Bold's real webhook spec was never confirmable (JS-rendered docs returned no usable content) so BoldPaymentProvider.parse_webhook_event always raises rather than pretend to verify something unconfirmed - do not treat Bold as production-ready without first getting its real docs.
